name: ANSI/IEEE multi-conductor cable symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented outline or bracket grouping several conductors to show they belong to one multi-conductor cable.
description: US-practice schematics group conductors of one cable with an enclosing outline, a bracket or an oval drawn across the conductor lines, usually with the cable number beside it. It lets the reader see which wires travel together between enclosures.

This illustration explains the convention rather than reproducing the IEEE graphic. The grouping implies no shield. Cable conductor count, gauge and insulation rating come from the cable schedule, and spare conductors are often not drawn.
readingNotes: Read the cable number next to the grouping.
drawingChecklist: Tag every grouping with the cable number.
Use the same tag across sheets.
Record gauge and spares in the schedule.
distinction: A cable grouping shows shared jacket only; a shielded cable form adds a conductive shield.
